heading: Schedule for Rating Disabilities (1945 Looseleaf Edition)
federal_register_citation: 29 FR 6718 (May 22, 1964 republication of 1945 VASRD; 38 C.F.R. § 3.952 & Part 4 App. A)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Although titled the '1945 Schedule for Rating Disabilities,' the baseline post-WWII VASRD took effect on April 1, 1946 (38 C.F.R. § 3.952; Part 4, Appendix A) and was codified in the Federal Register on May 22, 1964 (29 FR 6718). Protected pre-readjustment awards are governed by 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.951(a), 3.952, and 3.953.

heading: Pub. L. 85-56 and Pub. L. 85-857
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implements statutory savings clauses of section 2316(b), Pub. L. 85-56 (protecting compensation payable on December 31, 1957) and sections 10–11, Pub. L. 85-857 (protecting benefits payable or entitled on December 31, 1958) absent fraud, misrepresentation, or CUE.

heading: Pub. L. 85-56 and Pub. L. 85-857 (Current Print Text)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implements statutory savings clauses of section 2316(b), Pub. L. 85-56 (protecting compensation payable on December 31, 1957) and sections 10–11, Pub. L. 85-857 (protecting benefits payable or entitled on December 31, 1958) absent fraud, misrepresentation, or CUE.

heading: Report of examination or hospitalization as claim for increase or to reopen
applicability_and_transition_notes: Treated VA or uniformed-services outpatient examination or hospital admission reports for an already service-connected disability (including 0% noncompensable SC) as an automatic informal claim for increase. Remains fully operative when auditing pre-March 24, 2015 medical reports in CUE or pending-claim litigation.

heading: How to file a claim (Standard Claims and Appeals Forms; Repeal of § 3.157)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Prospective only from March 24, 2015: replaced non-form informal claims under former § 3.155(a) and repealed § 3.157 in its entirety, substituting the Intent to File (VA Form 21-0966) and standardized claim forms (VA Form 21-526EZ). Does not extinguish informal claims received before March 24, 2015 (Shea v. Wilkie).

heading: Stabilization of disability evaluations
applicability_and_transition_notes: Governs all evaluations in effect at the same level for 5 years or more (§ 3.344(c)). Any rating reduction violating § 3.344(a)–(b) (requiring full-and-complete examination review and sustained improvement under the ordinary conditions of life) is void ab initio (Brown v. Brown, 5 Vet. App. 413 (1993)).

heading: Stabilization of disability evaluations (Current Print Text)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Governs all evaluations in effect at the same level for 5 years or more (§ 3.344(c)). Any rating reduction violating § 3.344(a)–(b) (requiring full-and-complete examination review and sustained improvement under the ordinary conditions of life) is void ab initio (Brown v. Brown, 5 Vet. App. 413 (1993)).

heading: Service connection
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implements 38 U.S.C. § 1159 (statutory 10-year protection effective Jan. 1, 1962 under Pub. L. 86-501). Computed from the effective date of service connection to the effective date of the severance rating after full § 3.105(d) 60-day notice compliance.

heading: Preservation of disability ratings
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implements 38 U.S.C. § 1155 (no reduction due to VASRD readjustment absent actual medical improvement, § 3.951(a)) and 38 U.S.C. § 110 (continuous 20-year disability evaluation protected against reduction absent fraud, § 3.951(b)).

heading: Preservation of disability ratings (Current Print Text)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implements 38 U.S.C. § 1155 (no reduction due to VASRD readjustment absent actual medical improvement, § 3.951(a)) and 38 U.S.C. § 110 (continuous 20-year disability evaluation protected against reduction absent fraud, § 3.951(b)).

heading: Revision of decisions (Reduction in evaluation—compensation; Predetermination hearings)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Added § 3.105(i) predetermination hearing rights (30-day request window freezes benefits pending hearing and final decision) alongside § 3.105(e)'s 60-day advance notice and 60-day post-final-notice effective-date buffer. Noncompliance voids the reduction ab initio (Stern v. McDonough).

heading: Failure to report for Department of Veterans Affairs examination (Pre-1991 Running Awards Rule)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Applied strictly to beneficiaries with ongoing/running awards who failed to report for a scheduled reexamination; silent regarding original compensation claims (Wamhoff v. Brown, 8 Vet. App. 517 (1996); 55 FR 49520). Pull print 1989/1990 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.329 and 3.655 before filing pre-Dec. 31, 1990 CUE.

heading: Failure to report for Department of Veterans Affairs examination
applicability_and_transition_notes: Enacted effective December 31, 1990 (note: often confused with 55 FR 31579, Aug. 3, 1990, which amended § 4.16(a) TDIU). Mandated rating original compensation claims on the evidence of record (§ 3.655(b) sentence 1), denying reopened/increase claims (§ 3.655(b) sentence 2), and issuing 60-day pretermination notice on running awards (§ 3.655(c)).

heading: Failure to report for Department of Veterans Affairs examination
applicability_and_transition_notes: AMA conforming amendment effective February 19, 2019 replacing 'reopened claim' with 'supplemental claim' in § 3.655(b); preserves all substantive original-claim and running-award rules.

heading: New and material evidence (Supplemental report from service department)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Construed in Vigil v. Peake, 22 Vet. App. 63 (2008): operated alongside former § 3.400(q)(2) to authorize reconsideration and retroactive effective dates back to the original claim upon receipt of misplaced/corrected official service department records.

heading: New evidence — Service department records
applicability_and_transition_notes: Clarified § 3.156(c)(1)–(4) (proposed June 20, 2005 at 70 FR 35388; final effective Oct. 6, 2006), consolidating former § 3.400(q)(2) into § 3.156(c)(3) and explicitly covering unit/declassified/DoD records notwithstanding finality or AMA effective-date limits.

heading: Awards under the Nehmer Court Orders — Verbatim Excerpt: § 3.816(f)(1)–(4) (2003–2021 Prior-Release Bar)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Codified Nehmer class-action effective-date and estate/survivor payment rules displacing § 3.114(a) limits for covered Agent Orange presumptions (claims filed or denied on/after Sept. 25, 1985).

heading: Awards under the Nehmer Court Orders — Verbatim Excerpt: § 3.816(f)(1)–(4) (Post-Dec. 2, 2021 Payee Rule)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Removed the final sentence of § 3.816(f)(3) effective December 2, 2021 pursuant to N.D. Cal. enforcement orders, requiring full retroactive Nehmer payment to newly identified eligible payees even where VA previously paid another payee.

heading: DIC benefits for survivors of certain veterans rated totally disabled at time of death (1978–1989 Original Text Prior to 'For Any Reason' Clause)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implemented 38 U.S.C. § 1318 (formerly § 410(b), Pub. L. 95-479 eff. Oct. 1, 1978; 'for any reason' clause added by Pub. L. 100-687, § 1403 and codified at 54 FR 31829, Aug. 2, 1989 — note that 55 FR 8141, Mar. 7, 1990 amended § 3.32 foreign currency, NOT § 3.22). Construed in Green v. Brown, 10 Vet. App. 111 (1997) to allow open-ended posthumous hypothetical entitlement until superseded on Jan. 21, 2000.

heading: DIC benefits for survivors of certain veterans rated totally disabled at time of death — Verbatim Excerpt: § 3.22(a) ('For Any Reason' Era, 1989–2000)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implemented 38 U.S.C. § 1318 (formerly § 410(b), Pub. L. 95-479 eff. Oct. 1, 1978; 'for any reason' clause added by Pub. L. 100-687, § 1403 and codified at 54 FR 31829, Aug. 2, 1989 — note that 55 FR 8141, Mar. 7, 1990 amended § 3.32 foreign currency, NOT § 3.22). Construed in Green v. Brown, 10 Vet. App. 111 (1997) to allow open-ended posthumous hypothetical entitlement until superseded on Jan. 21, 2000.

heading: DIC benefits for survivors of certain veterans rated totally disabled at time of death
applicability_and_transition_notes: Issued effective immediately January 21, 2000 to abrogate Green v. Brown by restricting 'entitled to receive' to lifetime total ratings, lifetime-claim CUE (§ 3.22(b)(1)), or specified withholding/nonpayment categories; upheld in NOVA II, 314 F.3d 1373 (Fed. Cir. 2003), Rodriguez v. Peake, 511 F.3d 1147 (Fed. Cir. 2008) (applying rule to claims pending on Jan. 21, 2000), and Tarver v. Shinseki, 557 F.3d 1371 (Fed. Cir. 2009). Also added 1-year Former POW rule at 65 FR 43699 (retroactively eff. Nov. 30, 1999 per Pub. L. 106-117).

heading: DIC benefits for survivors of certain veterans rated totally disabled at time of death (2005–2012 § 3.22(b)(2) Service-Record Rule Prior to POW Date Removal)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Added § 3.22(b)(2) effective Dec. 2, 2005 following NOVA I/II, allowing posthumous retroactive total disability via newly associated service department records (§ 3.156(c) / former § 3.400(q)(2)). Amended July 10, 2012 (77 FR 40525, applicable to DIC claims pending or filed on/after Oct. 1, 2011 per Pub. L. 111-275, § 603) to delete 'who died after September 30, 1999' from the 1-year Former POW provision in § 3.22(a)(2)(iii).

heading: DIC benefits for survivors of certain veterans rated totally disabled at time of death (Current Text)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Added § 3.22(b)(2) effective Dec. 2, 2005 following NOVA I/II, allowing posthumous retroactive total disability via newly associated service department records (§ 3.156(c) / former § 3.400(q)(2)). Amended July 10, 2012 (77 FR 40525, applicable to DIC claims pending or filed on/after Oct. 1, 2011 per Pub. L. 111-275, § 603) to delete 'who died after September 30, 1999' from the 1-year Former POW provision in § 3.22(a)(2)(iii).

heading: Reevaluation of Claims for Dependency and Indemnity Compensation
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implements 38 U.S.C. § 1305 (enacted by Pub. L. 117-168, § 204, 136 Stat. 1776, statutory trigger Aug. 10, 2022). Published Nov. 24, 2023, effective January 23, 2024. Mandates that previously denied DIC claims re-elected under a post-Aug. 10, 2022 new or modified presumption (including PACT § 404 hypertension/MGUS) take effect 'notwithstanding section 5110' as if the presumption had been in effect on the submission date of the original denied DIC claim (§ 3.33(d)(1)).

heading: Cause of death
applicability_and_transition_notes: Governs all direct (principal, § 3.312(b)) and contributory (§ 3.312(c)(1)–(4)) service-connected death claims under 38 U.S.C. § 1310, including the assumed-debilitation rule where an active vital-organ disability is rated 100% disabling (§ 3.312(c)(3)).

heading: Cause of death (Current Print Text)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Governs all direct (principal, § 3.312(b)) and contributory (§ 3.312(c)(1)–(4)) service-connected death claims under 38 U.S.C. § 1310, including the assumed-debilitation rule where an active vital-organ disability is rated 100% disabling (§ 3.312(c)(3)).

heading: Reinstatement of benefits eligibility based upon terminated marital relationships (Age 57 DIC & Age 55 CHAMPVA Remarriage Rules)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Conformed § 3.55(a)(9) (Pub. L. 107-330 age-55 CHAMPVA eff. Feb. 4, 2003) and § 3.55(a)(10) (Pub. L. 108-183, § 101 age-57 DIC, DEA, and VA home-loan retention for remarriages on or after January 1, 2004, with a Dec. 16, 2004 retroactive application window for pre-Dec. 16, 2003 age-57 remarriages). Regulatory publication and effective date was May 19, 2006.

heading: Reinstatement of benefits eligibility based upon terminated marital relationships — Statutory Age-55 DIC Remarriage Lag Window (Pub. L. 116-315, § 2009)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Statutory lag period (Jan. 5, 2021 – Nov. 14, 2022): Pub. L. 116-315, § 2009 lowered the remarriage age threshold for retaining Chapter 13 DIC from age 57 to age 55 for remarriages occurring on or after January 5, 2021, superseding the lagging age-57 print text of § 3.55 prior to the November 15, 2022 conforming CFR rule (87 FR 68360).

heading: Reinstatement of benefits eligibility based upon terminated marital relationships (Age 55 DIC Remarriage Update)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Updated § 3.55(a)(9)–(11) effective Nov. 15, 2022 to conform CFR text with Pub. L. 116-315, § 2009 (134 Stat. 4932, 4978, enacted Jan. 5, 2021), lowering the remarriage age threshold for retaining Chapter 13 DIC from age 57 to age 55 for remarriages occurring on or after January 5, 2021 (while DEA Chapter 35 and Chapter 37 home loans remain at age 57 under § 3.55(a)(10), and remarriages between Jan. 1, 2004 and Jan. 4, 2021 remain governed by age 57).

heading: Entitlement under 38 U.S.C. 5121 to benefits due and unpaid upon death — Verbatim Excerpt: § 3.1000(a) Two-Year Cap
applicability_and_transition_notes: Restricted accrued periodic benefits due and unpaid at death 'for a period not to exceed 2 years prior to the last date of entitlement' (unless Nehmer § 3.816(f) applied). Repealed by Pub. L. 108-183, § 104 for deaths on or after Dec. 16, 2003 (and claims pending on Dec. 16, 2003).

heading: Entitlement under 38 U.S.C. 5121 to benefits due and unpaid upon death (2003–2015 Uncapped Rule Prior to § 3.1000(d)(4))
applicability_and_transition_notes: Conformed § 3.1000(a) effective Dec. 29, 2006 to Pub. L. 108-183, § 104 (statutory repeal of the 2-year accrued-benefits cap effective Dec. 16, 2003 for deaths on/after Dec. 16, 2003 or claims pending on that date) and codified § 3.1000(d)(4) constructive VA-possession definition of 'evidence in the file at date of death.'

heading: Entitlement under 38 U.S.C. 5121 to benefits due and unpaid upon death (Current Text Including § 3.1000(d)(4))
applicability_and_transition_notes: Conformed § 3.1000(a) effective Dec. 29, 2006 to Pub. L. 108-183, § 104 (statutory repeal of the 2-year accrued-benefits cap effective Dec. 16, 2003 for deaths on/after Dec. 16, 2003 or claims pending on that date) and codified § 3.1000(d)(4) constructive VA-possession definition of 'evidence in the file at date of death.'

heading: Substitution under 38 U.S.C. 5121A following death of a claimant
federal_register_citation: 79 FR 52977, 52982 (Sept. 5, 2014) (companion Board rule 38 C.F.R. § 20.1302 amended at 84 FR 138, 191, Jan. 18, 2019)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Operationalizes 38 U.S.C. § 5121A (enacted by Pub. L. 110-389, § 212 with statutory effective date October 10, 2008 for deaths on/after Oct. 10, 2008; 6-year interim period Oct. 10, 2008 – Oct. 5, 2014 governed by statute and Fast Letter 10-30). Final rule published Sept. 5, 2014, effective October 6, 2014; upheld in NOVA v. Sec'y, 809 F.3d 1359 (Fed. Cir. 2016). Note AMA lag nuance: 84 FR 138 (Jan. 18, 2019, eff. Feb. 19, 2019) amended companion Board rule § 20.1302 (84 FR 191) rather than § 3.1010 (84 FR 172 added §§ 3.2501–3.2601), leaving legacy 'notice of disagreement' phrasing in § 3.1010(g)(1).

heading: Character of discharge (1963–2022 Sub-Amendments Prior to Space Force Nomenclature)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Structured summary for pre-May 3, 2022 COD decisions (e.g., 1978 Pub. L. 95-126 special-upgrade bars at 43 FR 15153 and 1982 entry-level uncharacterized separation additions). Consult the contemporaneous annual GovInfo print 38 C.F.R. § 3.12 edition before pleading CUE on a pre-May 3, 2022 decision.

heading: Character of discharge (2022–2024 Pre-Overhaul Print Text)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Governs CUE motions attacking final COD denials adjudicated prior to June 25, 2024. Imposed five regulatory bars under § 3.12(d)(1)–(5) (including former (d)(5) aggravated homosexual acts), restricted compelling-circumstances mitigation strictly to 180+ day continuous AWOL under § 3.12(c)(6), and codified BCMR/DRB/Pub. L. 95-126 upgrade rules at former § 3.12(e)–(j) and uncharacterized separations at former § 3.12(k).

heading: Benefit eligibility based on character of discharge
applicability_and_transition_notes: Retitled § 3.12 and overhauled regulatory COD bars effective June 25, 2024: split § 3.12(d) into non-mitigable bars under § 3.12(d)(1)(i)–(ii) (discharge in lieu of GCM; mutiny or spying) and mitigable bars under § 3.12(d)(2)(i)–(ii) (moral turpitude; objective 2-yr/5-yr MCM willful and persistent misconduct), repealed former § 3.12(d)(5), added § 3.12(e) Compelling circumstances exception covering § 3.12(c)(6) prolonged AWOL and § 3.12(d)(2) misconduct, and redesignated former paragraphs (e)–(k) as (f)–(l). Explicit applicability rule (89 FR 32361): applies to claims received on/after June 25, 2024 or pending before VA, CAVC, or the Federal Circuit on June 25, 2024; liberalizing awards under 38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a) cannot precede June 25, 2024.

heading: Discharge to change status
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implements 38 U.S.C. § 101(18)(B) (codified in § 3.13(c) at 43 FR 15154, Apr. 11, 1978 pursuant to Pub. L. 95-126; VAOPGCPREC 10-96): treats an enlisted service member who completed an obligated period of active service eligible for an OTD discharge and immediately reenlisted without a physical break as unconditionally discharged from the prior enlistment, insulating benefits earned in the earlier enlistment from a dishonorable/OTH termination in a subsequent enlistment.

heading: Discharge to change status (Current Print Text)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implements 38 U.S.C. § 101(18)(B) (codified in § 3.13(c) at 43 FR 15154, Apr. 11, 1978 pursuant to Pub. L. 95-126; VAOPGCPREC 10-96): treats an enlisted service member who completed an obligated period of active service eligible for an OTD discharge and immediately reenlisted without a physical break as unconditionally discharged from the prior enlistment, insulating benefits earned in the earlier enlistment from a dishonorable/OTH termination in a subsequent enlistment.

heading: Determinations of insanity
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implements 38 U.S.C. § 5303(b) (formerly § 3103(b)). Establishes VA's broad, non-criminal definition of disease-induced insanity (§ 3.354(a); Zang v. Brown, 8 Vet. App. 246 (1995); Gardner v. Shinseki, 22 Vet. App. 415 (2009); VAOPGCPREC 20-97), removing all statutory and regulatory COD bars—including General Court-Martial sentences—when the veteran was insane at the time of the offense(s) leading to discharge.

heading: General — Correction of military records
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implements 38 U.S.C. § 5110(i) (Pub. L. 87-825) setting the effective date of awards based on 10 U.S.C. §§ 1552 (BCMR/BCNR) or 1553 (DRB) record corrections or discharge upgrades at the latest of: (1) date application for correction was filed with the service department, (2) date of receipt of prior disallowed VA claim, or (3) 1 year prior to reopening of disallowed claim (subject to § 3.156(c)(3) interplay where pre-existing service records also accompany the claim).

heading: Duty periods
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implements 38 U.S.C. §§ 101(21)–(24) and 106(c)–(d) governing Active Duty (§ 3.6(b)), Active Duty for Training (§ 3.6(c), requiring in-service disease or injury to achieve veteran status; Biggins v. Derwinski, 1 Vet. App. 474 (1991); Smith v. Shinseki, 24 Vet. App. 40 (2010); Donnellan v. Shinseki, 24 Vet. App. 167 (2010)), Inactive Duty Training (§ 3.6(a)(3), (d)), and portal-to-portal travel (§ 3.6(e)). Amended Sept. 21, 2001 (66 FR 48558, 48560), retroactively effective November 1, 2000 per Pub. L. 106-419, § 301, to cover acute myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest, and cerebrovascular accident ('covered disease') occurring during IADT or direct travel to/from ADT or IADT.

heading: Duty periods (Current Print Text)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Implements 38 U.S.C. §§ 101(21)–(24) and 106(c)–(d) governing Active Duty (§ 3.6(b)), Active Duty for Training (§ 3.6(c), requiring in-service disease or injury to achieve veteran status; Biggins v. Derwinski, 1 Vet. App. 474 (1991); Smith v. Shinseki, 24 Vet. App. 40 (2010); Donnellan v. Shinseki, 24 Vet. App. 167 (2010)), Inactive Duty Training (§ 3.6(a)(3), (d)), and portal-to-portal travel (§ 3.6(e)). Amended Sept. 21, 2001 (66 FR 48558, 48560), retroactively effective November 1, 2000 per Pub. L. 106-419, § 301, to cover acute myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest, and cerebrovascular accident ('covered disease') occurring during IADT or direct travel to/from ADT or IADT.

heading: Line of duty and misconduct (Abuse of alcohol or drugs) & Secondary Aggravation
applicability_and_transition_notes: Paragraph § 3.301(d) was added May 24, 1995 (60 FR 27407, 27408) implementing OBRA 1990 (Pub. L. 101-508, § 8052) to bar direct line-of-duty SC for primary alcohol/drug abuse on claims filed after October 31, 1990. In Allen v. Principi, 237 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2001), the Federal Circuit held OBRA 1990 does not bar secondary SC under § 3.310 for alcohol/drug abuse proximately caused or aggravated by a service-connected disability; VA codified § 3.310(b) secondary aggravation on Sept. 7, 2006 (71 FR 52744, 52747, effective October 10, 2006). (Citation note: neither 71 FR 44918, Aug. 8, 2006 nor 66 FR 18195, Apr. 6, 2001 tobacco rule enacted § 3.301(d) or the Allen secondary rule.)

heading: Total disability ratings for compensation based on unemployability of the individual
applicability_and_transition_notes: Established the 60% single / 70%-40% combined schedular thresholds, (1)–(5) single-disability aggregation rules, and § 4.16(b) extraschedular referral, governing § 4.16(a)–(b) continuously until the Sept. 4, 1990 Census poverty-threshold amendment (55 FR 31580).

heading: Total disability ratings for compensation based on unemployability of the individual (70% Mental Disorder Rule)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Mandated assigning a 100% schedular mental evaluation where the veteran's only compensable service-connected disability was a 70% mental disorder precluding substantially gainful employment (Johnson v. Brown, 7 Vet. App. 95 (1994)). Repealed effective Nov. 7, 1996.

heading: Total disability ratings for compensation based on unemployability of the individual (1990–2014 'Compensation and Pension Service' Print Text)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Added the marginal-employment Census Bureau poverty-threshold test and protected-environment (family business / sheltered workshop) facts-found rule to § 4.16(a) effective September 4, 1990. Karnas v. Derwinski governs claims pending across the Sept. 4, 1990 transition.

heading: Total disability ratings for compensation based on unemployability of the individual (Current 'Director, Compensation Service' Print Text)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Added the marginal-employment Census Bureau poverty-threshold test and protected-environment (family business / sheltered workshop) facts-found rule to § 4.16(a) effective September 4, 1990. Karnas v. Derwinski governs claims pending across the Sept. 4, 1990 transition.

heading: Schedule of ratings—mental disorders (General Rating Formula for Psychoneurotic Disorders)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Added the 70% evaluation tier to the Psychoneurotic General Rating Formula (DC 9400–9411, including PTSD) effective Feb. 3, 1988. Governs pre-Nov. 7, 1996 CUE claims; Karnas governs claims pending across Nov. 7, 1996.

heading: Schedule of ratings—Mental disorders (DSM-IV General Rating Formula)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Consolidated psychotic, organic, and psychoneurotic schedules into the unified General Rating Formula for Mental Disorders (0/10/30/50/70/100%) and repealed former § 4.16(c) effective November 7, 1996.

heading: Schedule of ratings—Mental disorders (DSM-5 Nomenclature Update)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Adopted DSM-5 diagnostic nomenclature and removed Global Assessment of Functioning (GAF) references effective August 4, 2014 while retaining the 1996 General Rating Formula symptom tiers verbatim. (Note: Feb. 15, 2022 proposed rule 87 FR 8498, RIN 2900-AQ82, remains unfinalized).

heading: Schedule for Rating Disabilities: Mental Disorders — Five-Domain Formula (Proposed Rule — Not Enacted)
applicability_and_transition_notes: QUARANTINED UNFINALIZED PROPOSAL: Notice of Proposed Rulemaking published February 15, 2022 (87 FR 8498, RIN 2900-AQ82) proposing a 5-domain General Rating Formula for Mental Disorders and eliminating the 0% mental evaluation tier. Remains proposed / not enacted law and must NEVER be cited as binding regulation.

heading: Factors to be considered in the evaluation of disabilities residual to healed wounds involving muscle groups due to gunshot or other trauma
applicability_and_transition_notes: Governs all muscle-injury CUE motions attacking rating decisions rendered prior to July 3, 1997. Did not yet contain the bright-line § 4.56(b) 'shall be evaluated as no less than a moderate injury' clause added in 1997.

heading: Evaluation of muscle disabilities
applicability_and_transition_notes: Enacted §§ 4.55–4.56 overhaul effective July 3, 1997, codifying the mandatory moderate-injury floor for through-and-through muscle damage (§ 4.56(b)) and severe-injury presumption for open comminuted fractures with muscle/tendon damage (§ 4.56(a)).

heading: Schedule of ratings—skin (1946–1978 Original Looseleaf & 29 FR 6718 Scar Baseline Prior to 43 FR 45362)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Structured summary for pre-October 2, 1978 scar and disfigurement ratings under the original 1945 Schedule (29 FR 6718) prior to the 43 FR 45362 revision. Pull contemporaneous pre-1978 GovInfo print 38 C.F.R. § 4.118 before pleading CUE on a pre-October 2, 1978 decision.

heading: Schedule of ratings—skin (1978–2002 Qualitative Disfigurement & Single 10% DC 7804 Print Text)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Governs scar and disfigurement CUE motions attacking final rating decisions rendered from October 2, 1978 through August 29, 2002. Evaluated DC 7800 head/face/neck disfigurement on qualitative tiers (0/10/30/50%, with step-up note to 80%) and capped superficial painful scars under DC 7804 at a single 10% evaluation.

heading: Schedule of ratings—skin (DC 7800–7805 Scars & Disfigurement)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Replaced the 1978 (43 FR 45362) subjective disfigurement tiers with the 8 objective characteristics of disfigurement and an 80% ceiling under DC 7800 effective August 30, 2002; DC 7804 remained capped at a single 10% evaluation until Oct. 23, 2008.

heading: Schedule of ratings—skin (DC 7800–7805 Count-Based Painful/Unstable Scars)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Deleted DC 7803 and enacted count-based DC 7804 (1–2 = 10%, 3–4 = 20%, 5+ = 30%, +10% if both unstable and painful) effective October 23, 2008. Explicit applicability rule (73 FR 54708; 77 FR 2909): applies to claims received on/after Oct. 23, 2008, or pending claims where the veteran elects or receives a higher post-Oct. 23, 2008 staged evaluation.

heading: Schedule of ratings—skin (DC 7800–7805 Body Zones & Linear Scar Update)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Removed the 'nonlinear' restriction from DC 7801–7802 and codified 6 distinct non-head/face/neck body zones effective August 13, 2018. (Note: Sept. 29, 2025 proposed rule 90 FR 46542 on DC 7804 objective pain remains unfinalized).

heading: Schedule for Rating Disabilities: Skin — DC 7804 Objective Pain Note (Proposed Rule — Not Enacted)
applicability_and_transition_notes: QUARANTINED UNFINALIZED PROPOSAL: Notice of Proposed Rulemaking published September 29, 2025 (90 FR 46542) proposing to add a note to DC 7804 requiring objective confirmation of pain upon examination or demonstration. Remains unfinalized / not enacted law and must NEVER be cited as an active regulation.

heading: Schedule of ratings—musculoskeletal system (Pre-Sept. 23, 2002 Qualitative Spine & DC 5285–5295 Schedule)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Governs spine CUE motions attacking final rating decisions rendered prior to September 23, 2002 (and non-IVDS spine ratings through September 25, 2003): evaluated vertebral fracture residuals (DC 5285), ankylosis (DC 5286–5289), qualitative slight/moderate/severe limitation of motion (DC 5290–5292), recurring IVDS attacks (DC 5293), sacroiliac injury (DC 5294), and lumbosacral strain (DC 5295). For pre-2015 non-spine joint/prosthetic ratings, pull contemporaneous GovInfo print 38 C.F.R. § 4.71a.

heading: Schedule of ratings—musculoskeletal system (2002–2003 Interim DC 5293 Incapacitating-Episodes Rule + DC 5285–5295 Spine Schedule)
applicability_and_transition_notes: Replaced legacy DC 5293 recurring-attack tiers with the physician-prescribed bed-rest Incapacitating Episodes formula (10/20/40/60%) vs. combined orthopedic/neurologic evaluation effective Sept. 23, 2002, one year before the broader spine overhaul.

heading: Schedule of ratings—musculoskeletal system (General Rating Formula for Diseases and Injuries of the Spine)
